hero.headline: Major companies directed tariff refund money to executive bonuses, ProPublica investigation finds
hero.teaser: At least nine major companies receiving refunds after the Supreme Court struck down Trump-era tariffs directed portions of that money toward executive bonuses instead of consumer p
hero.body:
At least nine major companies receiving refunds after the Supreme Court struck down Trump-era tariffs directed portions of that money toward executive bonuses instead of consumer price relief, according to a ProPublica investigation published Monday. The investigation analyzed securities filings and earnings calls to identify companies that told consumers they had to raise prices because of tariffs but are now using refund money for leadership compensation.

Stanley Black & Decker, which makes vacuums, electric drills, and measuring tapes, is expected to receive at least $298 million in tariff reimbursements and indicated some will go to bonuses. The company told consumers it was forced to raise prices because of Trump's import fees. In financial disclosures, Stanley Black & Decker said the refund it received was partially offset by costs for variable incentive compensation, according to ProPublica.

TJX, the parent company of TJ Maxx and Marshalls, received $331 million in refunds and will accrue $112 million in year-end incentive compensation and discretionary bonuses for eligible associates globally because of the refunds, a company spokesperson confirmed to ProPublica. The spokesperson said the company has not disclosed details beyond that accrual because the fiscal year has not ended.

The Trump administration has refunded at least $100 billion to companies since August, about 60 percent of roughly $131 billion in tariffs collected, after the Supreme Court ruled that Trump's tariffs were illegal because they overstepped executive authority and should have required congressional approval. The administration has not specified which companies are receiving refunds despite requests for information. ProPublica found that almost all companies publicly planning to use reimbursements for customer refunds deal with other businesses rather than consumers directly, while some companies have remained vague about their plans for the money.

cards.headline: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and Netherlands to open migrant deportation hub in Rwanda in 2027
cards.body:
Five European Union countries announced plans to open a migrant deportation center in Rwanda next year, sparking criticism from Spain and human rights organizations over the legality and ethics of the arrangement. Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands said the return hub will be ready to accept transfers in 2027 and will apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation. The Dutch government said the facility will provide an alternative when deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin.

The five countries said the scheme is in line with EU and international law, but human rights groups disputed that claim. Human Rights Watch senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said Rwanda has a well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention and support for armed rebels in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The independent EU Agency for Fundamental Rights said any third country hosting a return hub should respect fundamental rights, including that people should not be sent to a country where they face serious risk of persecution.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez told Spanish broadcaster Telecinco that the plan had no future or humanity and was not the solution, according to AFP news agency. The arrangement follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside the bloc. At a joint press conference in Vienna, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean.

The plan differs from a British deal scrapped in 2024 that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have asylum claims processed. The new scheme will apply only to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations. Diplomatic sources told AFP the hub is expected to initially run as a pilot hosting about 100 people, with each nation possibly sending about 20 migrants. The Dutch government said the first phase will only return single men, with a focus on people from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda. Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta said the country is committed to working with European partners to provide a safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants.

cards.headline: UK set to sign Brexit food trade reset with EU, aiming for £5bn economic boost
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Andy Burnham plans to sign an agreement Friday ending post-Brexit food export barriers, but the deal includes an exit clause and limits UK regulatory influence.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham plans to sign an agreement Friday ending post-Brexit food export barriers, but the deal includes an exit clause and limits UK regulatory influence.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham will sign a Brexit reset agreement with the European Union on Friday that the government says could boost the economy by £5 billion annually and reduce household food costs. The deal would eliminate hundreds of pages of export forms and veterinary checks that have cost British businesses millions of pounds since Boris Johnson's 2020 Brexit agreement prioritized regulatory freedom over trade flow.

cards.headline: Tech leaders question circumstances of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation
cards.teaser: Prominent figures call for Huang's reinstatement amid unconfirmed spy allegations involving a former executive.
cards.body:
Prominent tech leaders are questioning the circumstances surrounding Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years, with many calling for his reinstatement. The resignation followed reporting that Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive with whom Huang allegedly had an affair, was a Chinese spy, though U.S. agencies have not confirmed this claim.

Venture capitalist David Sacks and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have expressed skepticism about the reporting, with Sacks saying U.S. officials cannot confirm the spy allegations. More than 185,000 people, including Elon Musk and several tech CEOs, have signed a letter demanding closer scrutiny of Huang's resignation and stating that suspicion alone is insufficient grounds for ending his leadership.

cards.headline: Patriots fear quarterback Drake Maye suffered fractured ankle that could end his season
cards.body:
The New England Patriots believe quarterback Drake Maye may have fractured his ankle during Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich, sources told ESPN. Maye could miss the remainder of the season after being sacked in the first quarter by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson, who suffered a torn ACL in his right knee while celebrating the play and will miss the rest of the year, sources told NFL Network.

Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told reporters Monday he did not expect Maye to play when New England returns from its bye week to face the Los Angeles Chargers, but declined to discuss specifics about the injury or timeline. Maye remained in Germany and did not travel back with the team as a precaution, Vrabel said during a radio interview. The coach added he does not anticipate seeking a quarterback replacement from outside the organization.

Maye was replaced Sunday by backup Tommy DeVito. The Patriots also have rookie Behren Morton, a seventh-round draft pick from Texas Tech, on the roster. Maye's streak of 43 consecutive starts, including playoffs, is the third longest among active NFL quarterbacks behind Buffalo's Josh Allen and Detroit's Jared Goff.

Hutchinson brought Maye down from behind, landing on the quarterback's lower leg. After leaping to celebrate the sack, Hutchinson landed awkwardly and immediately clutched his knee. Fox rules analyst Mike Pereira and the NFL's officiating rules analyst Walt Anderson both confirmed the tackle was not a hip-drop, which requires unweighting, swiveling, and landing on the back of the leg below the knee. No penalty was called on the play. Vrabel said he did not believe there was any ill intent.

cards.headline: Five factors behind the Chargers' 0-9 start and historically bad offense
cards.teaser: Los Angeles ranks 30th or worse in points, touchdowns, and efficiency under new coordinator Mike McDaniel.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are the only winless team in the NFL at 0-9 and rank 30th or worse in points, touchdowns, turnovers, and efficiency under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. Quarterback Justin Herbert has thrown 11 interceptions, tied for most in the league, while injuries and poor play along the offensive line have contributed to 31 sacks, second most in the NFL.

Running back Omarion Hampton is averaging under 4.0 yards per carry on zone plays, the scheme's foundation, while receiver Ladd McConkey has played just one full game due to injuries. The Chargers went 37 consecutive drives without a touchdown before scoring in the fourth quarter of their 44-22 loss to Houston in Week 10.

cards.headline: Littler hits triple-bull, but Price checkout doesn't add up
cards.teaser: Luke Littler produced a remarkable 150 checkout at the Grand Slam of Darts, while Gerwyn Price advanced despite a referee scoring error.
cards.body:
Luke Littler landed three darts on the bullseye for a 150 checkout in his 5-4 loss to Niels Zonneveld at the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton, though the 19-year-old still advanced from the group stage. Gerwyn Price defeated Sebastian Bialecki 5-2 but benefited from a referee error when he was incorrectly told he had 88 remaining instead of 78, leading him to score 145 and bust without penalty.

The Professional Darts Corporation said the leg result stood under Darts Regulation Authority rules because the error was not corrected before the next leg began. Price said he was unaware of the miscalculation until after the match.

cards.headline: Houthi rebels seize control of key Red Sea strait as Yemeni army withdraws to defend Aden
cards.teaser: Iran-backed Houthi rebels have taken full control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait and nearby offshore islands after forcing the army of Yemen's internationally recognized government to
cards.body:
Iran-backed Houthi rebels have taken full control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait and nearby offshore islands after forcing the army of Yemen's internationally recognized government to

The strait, which accounts for around 12 percent of global trade with 70 to 150 ships passing through daily, connects the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean. The Houthi advance follows the breakdown of a truce with Saudi Arabia in July and a failed government counter-offensive.

hero.headline: Forensic expert reviewing autopsy photos says Jeffrey Epstein was strangled, not suicide
hero.body:
A forensic expert has concluded that Jeffrey Epstein was killed in prison in 2019, contradicting the official ruling that his death was suicide. Professor Michael Freeman told BBC Newsnight that after reviewing autopsy files and photographs, he believes Epstein was strangled, most likely from behind. Freeman said the evidence includes a deep hemorrhage to Epstein's left shoulder, injuries consistent with being struck in the face, and apparent fingernail marks above the ligature mark on his neck that would be consistent with an attempt to remove a ligature during strangulation.

Freeman, who has served as a cause-of-death expert to state attorneys general in police custody cases including George Floyd, said he believed a ligature was used to strangle Epstein and then used to suspend the body from a bunk bed. He said the injuries and the way the body was found do not match the conclusion of suicide by hanging. Freeman obtained the files from Epstein's brother, Mark Epstein, who has maintained his brother was murdered. Freeman said his analysis was independent and unpaid, though it has not been peer-reviewed.

The official autopsy in 2019 concluded Epstein's injuries were consistent with suicide and showed no defensive wounds expected in a homicide. The medical examiner who performed the autopsy told the Department of Justice that the injuries were more consistent with suicide by hanging rather than homicide by strangulation. Chief Medical Examiner Barbara Sampson, who ruled the death a suicide, has previously said she stands firmly behind the determination.

Epstein was found dead on August 10, 2019, at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in New York while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges. His death came a month after he had been briefly placed on suicide watch. Epstein was convicted in 2008 of soliciting prostitution from a minor and was charged in 2019 with running a network of underage girls for sex.

cards.headline: Massachusetts judge sets March 2027 retrial for woman accused of killing three children after hung jury
cards.teaser: A Massachusetts judge set a March 29, 2027, trial date for Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of murdering her three children, after a jury deadlocked in her first trial in September.
cards.body:
A Massachusetts judge set a March 29, 2027, trial date for Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of murdering her three children, after a jury deadlocked in her first trial in September.

Judge William Sullivan rejected a defense motion last week to dismiss the case on double jeopardy grounds, clearing the way for the retrial. Prosecutors indicated they intend to seek a jury trial, which the defense interpreted as a signal that Clancy, 36, will again face first-degree murder charges, though the district attorney has not formally announced the charges.

hero.headline: Chase, Wells Fargo, Bank of America customers report service outages
hero.body:
Thousands of customers at major U.S. banks reported trouble accessing services Monday afternoon, with Chase Bank citing a software bug in its hardware systems as a likely cause. Chase, the largest banking institution in the country, said the issue was temporary and not systemic or cyber-related. The outages also affected Wells Fargo and Bank of America, though Chase said the bug in its systems may have impacted other banks as well.

Nearly 5,000 reports of Chase Bank service disruptions appeared on the Downdetector website. Chase told customers that some transactions were taking longer than usual to complete but that they still had access to their accounts and funds. The bank, a subsidiary of JP Morgan Chase, serves more than 86 million customers at 5,000 branches across the United States and 7.4 million small businesses. It is also the top credit card issuer in the country.

US Bank said some of its systems were not directly affected, but clients using Zelle, a digital payment platform, received error messages saying their payments could not be sent. Zelle said its service was operating normally and that issues at other banks could be affecting payments. Customers also reported problems with Truist, PNC and Capital One, though those companies said they had not been impacted.

By early Monday evening, problems appeared to be easing for many customers. As of 6 p.m. Eastern Time, Chase, Bank of America and US Bank had seen a decline in the number of reported outages. The exact nature of the software bug remained unclear.

cards.headline: Software bug disrupts Chase banking nationwide, slowing Zelle and transactions at other banks
cards.teaser: A software bug in JPMorgan Chase's on-premise hardware systems disrupted banking services nationwide on Monday, affecting both online access and in-branch transactions and causing
cards.body:
A software bug in JPMorgan Chase's on-premise hardware systems disrupted banking services nationwide on Monday, affecting both online access and in-branch transactions and causing

The bank said the issue was not cyber-related and that all customers retained access to their accounts and funds, though servicing some customers was taking longer than usual. Chase said it was working to resolve the problem by the end of the day.

hero.headline: Cybersecurity firm Infoblox confirms breach through compromised SharePoint migration vendor
hero.body:
Infoblox, a cybersecurity and networking services company, confirmed hackers accessed company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor. The company said it is investigating unauthorized access to certain company information and has activated incident response procedures to contain the breach.

The breach involved a vendor that provides SharePoint data migration services, according to two people with knowledge of the incident. SharePoint is web-based software that companies use to share and host internal files and documents. One person familiar with the matter said sensitive customer data was taken in the breach.

Infoblox, which provides domain name resolution and identity and user access management services to companies, said it is working with outside cybersecurity experts to investigate and address confirmed risks. The company has not named the compromised vendor, though one person with knowledge of the incident said Infoblox has terminated its work with that vendor. Public internet records show Infoblox hosts much of its files, emails, and infrastructure with Microsoft, including a SharePoint server accessible through the company's single sign-on provider.

An Infoblox spokesperson said the company has no indication that any of its products, cloud services, software updates, or build-and-release processes were involved in the breach. The company did not disclose how many customers were affected or whether hackers contacted the company with demands.

cards.headline: Microsoft says dormant bug, traffic shifts caused 24-hour Microsoft 365 outage
cards.teaser: A preliminary incident report attributes last week's nearly day-long service disruption to a latent software defect introduced in July, combined with routine network maintenance.
cards.body:
Microsoft released a preliminary incident report attributing last week's nearly 24-hour Microsoft 365 and Exchange outage to a dormant software bug combined with routine traffic shifts. The company said a defect deployed to its cloud gateway in July could cause servers to exhaust CPU and memory resources under certain conditions, but the bug went undetected because testing hardware was less powerful than some production systems.

The outage began November 12 when standard network maintenance shifted Teams traffic to the primary gateway already handling Exchange Online access. The combined load triggered the latent bug, causing affected servers to refuse new connections. Microsoft said the incident lasted from November 12 at 16:20 UTC to November 13 at 16:10 UTC and was not related to cyberattacks.

cards.headline: Apple unveils new macOS security controls to limit AI agents' access to user data
cards.teaser: New settings split permissions and require explicit approval as AI agents demand broader system access.
cards.body:
New settings split permissions and require explicit approval as AI agents demand broader system access.

Apple announced changes to macOS security controls aimed at protecting user data from AI agents that request full disk access. The company warned that granting such access puts all data on a Mac at risk as AI agents increasingly operate across files and applications.

cards.headline: US hyperscale data centers consumed as much electricity as many mid-sized countries, study finds
cards.teaser: The facilities burned through 82 terawatt-hours annually and produced emissions comparable to Denmark's carbon footprint.
cards.body:
Hyperscale data centers in the United States consumed approximately 82 terawatt-hours of electricity between May 2024 and April 2025, more than 148 individual nations including Austria and Venezuela, according to a study published in Nature Sustainability. Researchers used satellite imagery to identify 403 hyperscale facilities and estimated their power consumption based on electrical capacity.

The electricity demand produced 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions, comparable to Denmark's annual carbon footprint. About 54 percent of the electricity consumed by the facilities came from gas and coal. Researchers noted that two data centers using identical amounts of electricity can have dramatically different environmental impacts depending on their local power grids.

cards.headline: Hacker who leaked 90 unreleased Grand Theft Auto VI videos pleads guilty
cards.teaser: Arion Kurtaj, member of the Lapsus$ cybercrime group, admitted to breaching Rockstar Games and other major companies while on bail in a hotel.
cards.body:
Arion Kurtaj, a member of the Lapsus$ cybercrime group who leaked 90 videos of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022, pleaded guilty on Monday, according to the UK's Crown Prosecution Service. Kurtaj, now 21, was charged with hacking BT/EE in 2021 and placed in a hotel in September 2022 for his own protection.

While on bail, Kurtaj breached his conditions and hacked Rockstar Games, Uber, and Revolut using a mobile phone, the hotel television's Wi-Fi, and a streaming device. He was sentenced to life in a secure hospital in December 2023, then moved to prison in January after being deemed fit for trial. Kurtaj is scheduled to be sentenced on November 23rd.

cards.headline: Intel shareholders file class-action lawsuit over alleged failure to disclose PC sales impact
cards.teaser: Suit claims company concealed slump's severity before 28.6 percent stock drop in October.
cards.body:
Intel, Chief Executive Officer Lip-Bu Tan, and Chief Financial Officer David Zinsner face a class-action lawsuit accusing them of misleading shareholders about the severity of a PC sales slump. The complaint, filed Friday in federal court in San Jose, California, alleges Intel made false and misleading statements between July 23 and October 29 by failing to disclose the full impact of declining PC sales and supply constraints on the company's business.

Intel's stock dropped 28.6 percent on October 30. The plaintiffs, led by the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System, are seeking unspecified compensatory damages for shareholders during the period when the alleged misstatements occurred.

cards.headline: Philip Rivers introduced as NC State head coach, says alma mater was 'the only thing' he'd leave broadcast booth for
cards.teaser: The former NFL quarterback acknowledged his lack of coaching experience but said no other college job would have drawn him from broadcasting.
cards.body:
Philip Rivers was introduced as NC State's new head coach Monday, telling supporters that his alma mater was the only college job he would have accepted. Rivers, who has never coached at the college or NFL level, acknowledged his thin résumé but said his 17-year NFL career prepared him for the role and that he plans to surround himself with experienced assistants.

Rivers' contract will pay him $3.5 million per year. He said the figure reflects both his lack of coaching experience and the fact that he was only interested in one job. Rivers named former teammate Jatavis Sanders as general manager and said he would begin evaluating the roster and assembling a staff immediately.

cards.headline: SEC will not penalize LSU if it rosters St. John's transfer RJ Luis Jr.
cards.teaser: The conference said it will abide by a Louisiana judge's preliminary injunction protecting the school from punishment.
cards.body:
The conference said it will abide by a Louisiana judge's preliminary injunction protecting the school from punishment.

The SEC has told LSU it will not penalize the school if it adds former St. John's guard RJ Luis Jr.

cards.headline: Michigan State rises to No. 2 in AP poll after upsetting Duke
cards.teaser: The Spartans received three first-place votes following their victory over the then-No. 5 Blue Devils, while LSU returned to the rankings for the first time in four seasons.
cards.body:
Michigan State moved up three spots to No. 2 in the AP men's basketball poll released Monday after defeating then-No. 5 Duke 79-73. The Spartans received three first-place votes from the 59-person media panel behind Jeremy Fears Jr., who finished with 18 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds in the win. Michigan State is 4-0 under coach Tom Izzo in his 32nd season.

LSU entered the poll at No. 25 for the first time since the 2021-22 season after beating No. 22 Gonzaga 81-80 on Donovan Dent's last-second 3-pointer. Virginia moved into the top five at No. 4, while Texas Tech climbed seven spots to No. 9 following a win over previously third-ranked Illinois.

cards.headline: Indiana coach Cignetti criticizes CFP rankings after Hoosiers dropped to No. 9
cards.teaser: Curt Cignetti says skepticism of Indiana's 25-1 record fuels the team's motivation as they pursue another national title.
cards.body:
Indiana coach Curt Cignetti said Monday that his team's accomplishments continue to be unfairly discredited, criticizing the narrative surrounding the Hoosiers' schedule and opponents. The Hoosiers dropped five spots to No. 9 in the College Football Playoff rankings last week despite not playing Nov. 7, prompting Cignetti to question the selection process on social media Thursday.

Cignetti, whose team is 25-1, pointed to opponents' declining performance after facing Indiana, including No. 20 Ohio State, which lost its next two games after defeating the Hoosiers 19-15 on Nov. 17. "It feeds into our motivation and our chip," Cignetti said. "I'm 65 years old and I really don't give a s---." Indiana faces Washington this week and Purdue next week.

cards.headline: Texas quarterback Arch Manning to participate in senior day, undecided on future
cards.teaser: The fourth-year quarterback will take part in Saturday's ceremonies but has not determined whether he will return for his final season of eligibility.
cards.body:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning said Monday he will participate in Saturday's senior day ceremonies before the final home game against Arkansas, but has not decided his playing future. Manning, a fourth-year player, will have one season of college eligibility remaining and must choose whether to stay at Texas, transfer, or enter the NFL draft.

Manning is 20-5 as a starter and led the sixth-ranked Longhorns to a 22-21 win at LSU on Saturday, throwing the winning touchdown pass with three seconds remaining. Texas is on a four-game winning streak and in position to reach the College Football Playoff. Manning said he is focused on the current week and not thinking about his future.

cards.headline: Michigan State's Jeremy Fears Jr. tops early player of the year rankings
cards.teaser: The point guard impressed in a Champions Classic win over Duke, outpacing candidates from Florida, Arizona, BYU and UConn.
cards.body:
Michigan State point guard Jeremy Fears Jr. leads early national player of the year rankings after two weeks of the 2026-27 college basketball season. Fears posted 18 points, seven rebounds and 11 assists in the Spartans' 79-73 Champions Classic victory over Duke on November 10, with Duke coach Jon Scheyer acknowledging that Fears controlled the entire game.

Florida forward Thomas Haugh ranks second, followed by Arizona's Ivan Kharchenkov, BYU guard Robert Wright III and UConn point guard Silas Demary Jr. The race is expected to remain wide open this season as revenue sharing and higher salary caps have brought deeper talent, including potential NBA draft picks returning and European professionals joining college programs.

hero.headline: Shakira, Drake, and Rosalía Among Latin Music Artists Featured in 2027 Grammy Nominations
hero.body:
The 2027 Grammy nominations highlight Latin music's continued prominence, with Spanish singer Rosalía earning the second-most nominations overall and a chance to follow Bad Bunny's historic 2026 Album of the Year win. If her album Lux wins the category, Rosalía would become the first woman to win Album of the Year with a Spanish-language project. Drake received a nomination for Best Latin Song for his feature on Karol G's "Ahí," marking a surprising recognition given his longstanding tensions with the Recording Academy and his decision to stop submitting his own work after a 2019 win.

Several Latin artists received their first Grammy nominations, including Colombian musician Ryan Castro, who earned two nods in Best Música Urbana Album for his solo album and a collaborative project with J Balvin. Argentine musician Milo J was nominated for Best Latin Song and Best Latin Rock or Alternative Album, while Venezuelan American singer Elena Rose secured her first nomination in the Best Latin Pop Album category.

The Best Latin Pop Album category drew criticism for grouping together artists with distinct musical styles under one umbrella. Nominees include Karol G, Mon Laferte, Carín León, Rawayana, and Elena Rose, with their albums spanning genres from alternative to norteño, salsa, and soul. Critics noted the category fails to properly honor the varied Latin genres the artists represent.

Latin music's global reach was reflected in nominations outside traditional Latin categories. Anitta's album Equilibrivm received a nomination for Best Global Music Album, while Shakira's World Cup song "Dai Dai" was nominated for Best Global Music Performance. Songwriter Edgar Barrera earned his third consecutive nomination for Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical, after losing in the category the previous two years.

cards.headline: Dolly Parton receives three posthumous Grammy nominations
cards.teaser: The country legend earned nods including one for a charity recording with goddaughter Miley Cyrus.
cards.body:
Dolly Parton received three posthumous Grammy nominations when the 69th annual awards nominees were announced Monday. The nominations include Best Country Duo/Group Performance for her rerecording of "Light of a Clear Blue Morning" featuring goddaughter Miley Cyrus, Reba McEntire, and Queen Latifah. The charity single raised funds for pediatric cancer research at Monroe Carell Jr. Children's Hospital at Vanderbilt in Nashville.

Cyrus reflected on social media about the nomination, writing that Parton "never made music for recognition but to make the world a happier place through her songs." Parton also earned nominations for "Butterfly" with Zac Brown Band and Best Audio Book for her 2025 memoir.

cards.headline: DJ John Summit criticizes Grammy dance nominations, draws backlash from producers
cards.teaser: The DJ called the dance categories a "joke" dominated by pop stars, prompting producers to defend their work.
cards.body:
DJ and producer John Summit criticized the Grammy Awards' dance and electronic music nominations, writing on social media that the categories featured "music industry fueled pop stars" with "zero respect for real electronic music & dj's." Summit, who released his second album earlier this year, said he would not submit to the Grammys again unless changes are made.

cards.headline: Judge dismisses four claims in Priscilla Presley fraud lawsuit, allows Lisa Marie death allegations
cards.teaser: A Los Angeles judge tossed four of 21 claims filed against Priscilla Presley by former business advisers but declined to remove allegations about Lisa Marie Presley's death.
cards.body:
A Los Angeles judge on Monday dismissed four of 21 claims against Priscilla Presley in a $50 million fraud lawsuit brought by former business advisers Brigitte Kruse and Kevin Fialko. Judge Mark Epstein ruled that claims Presley interfered with a cosmetics contract and improperly used her own name and likeness were not sufficiently supported by facts.

The judge refused to remove allegations that Presley prematurely ended life support for her daughter, Lisa Marie Presley, for financial gain. Lisa Marie died in 2023 after a small bowel obstruction. While calling portions of the complaint "gratuitous and mean-spirited," Epstein said striking the disputed language would make little difference because the claims were already public. Ten other claims related to fraud and breach of contract remain.

cards.headline: Spider-Man: Brand New Day extended cut to hit theaters in December
cards.teaser: The re-release includes previously cut footage, with Rosario Dawson set to appear as Night Nurse.
cards.body:
An extended cut of Spider-Man: Brand New Day will return to theaters in December, with tickets going on sale in November. The re-release includes previously removed footage, including a cameo by Rosario Dawson as Claire Temple, also known as Night Nurse. Dawson revealed in August that her scene had been cut from the original version.

The film opened in July and has grossed $2.5 billion worldwide, making it the third-highest-grossing movie of all time behind Avatar and Avengers: Endgame. It overtook Star Wars: The Force Awakens as the highest-grossing domestic film in history after 47 days in theaters.

cards.headline: Netflix orders limited series adaptation of Harlan Coben's The Innocent
cards.teaser: The streamer announced the project at the Texas Book Festival, marking its 15th collaboration with the bestselling author.
cards.body:
Netflix has ordered a limited series adaptation of Harlan Coben's novel The Innocent, the company's 15th project based on the author's work. The announcement came during Netflix's first appearance at the Texas Book Festival. The series will be written and executive produced by Robert Hull, Bryan Wynbrandt, and Steven Lilien, who previously created the Coben adaptation I Will Find You for Netflix.

The novel follows Matt Hunter, whose life unravels nine years after he accidentally killed a man while breaking up a fight. This marks the second adaptation of The Innocent for Netflix, following a 2021 Spanish-language version. Coben's Netflix projects have collectively generated over 450 million views.

cards.headline: Hulu renews legal drama Reasonable Doubt for fifth season
cards.teaser: The renewal comes ahead of the Season 4 finale, with the current season marking the show's most-watched to date.
cards.body:
Hulu and Onyx Collective have renewed Reasonable Doubt for a fifth season, with the announcement coming just before the legal drama's Season 4 finale. The show stars Emayatzy Corinealdi as Jax, a defense attorney navigating high-stakes cases while managing her law firm.

Season 4 is the series' most-watched season, with the show having been streamed for over 150 million hours globally since its 2022 debut. The fifth season will make Reasonable Doubt one of Hulu's longest-running scripted series. Raamla Mohamed Hunter created the show, with Kerry Washington among the executive producers.

hero.headline: Trump nominates OMB official Eric Ueland to head GAO watchdog agency
hero.teaser: President Donald Trump has nominated Eric Ueland as comptroller general and head of the Government Accountability Office, a position empowered to sue the administration on behalf o
hero.body:
President Donald Trump has nominated Eric Ueland as comptroller general and head of the Government Accountability Office, a position empowered to sue the administration on behalf of Congress. The nomination represents a push to confirm an ally before Democrats take control of Congress in January. Ueland currently serves as deputy director for management at the Office of Management and Budget, which has led efforts to withhold and cancel federal funding.

The Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee will hold a hearing on the nomination Thursday. Lawmakers in both parties have called for the GAO to challenge the Trump administration before the Supreme Court for withholding federal funds approved by Congress. The agency has issued more than a half-dozen findings of illegal impoundment of federal dollars since the start of Trump's second term but has not yet taken legal action.

Ueland has significant Capitol Hill experience as a former staff director for Senate Budget Committee Republicans under then-Chair Michael Enzi of Wyoming and chief of staff to former Republican Senate Majority Leader Bill Frist. He served as White House director of legislative affairs during the first Trump administration, where he brokered talks between then-Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin and senators on a Covid-19 economic relief package.

Democrats have criticized Republicans for what they call a sham confirmation process that breaks precedent for how the comptroller general is typically nominated. Some Republican senators, particularly those leaving office in January, could question whether it is appropriate to confirm a sitting executive branch official to a position responsible for investigating that same administration. The Supreme Court suggested last fall that the GAO is the only entity with standing to sue the Trump administration for violating the Impoundment Control Act. The agency has been operating under an acting comptroller general since last December.
